newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - MasterCard CEO sees huge opportunities.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - MasterCard CEO sees huge opportunities.

text.p: Use of plastic cards instead of cash and checks to pay for goods and services is a growth business worldwide, Robert Selander, new president and chief executive officer of MasterCard International said in an interview Wednesday.

Selander, who has been heading MasterCard's Europe, Middle East/Africa and Canada regions, was named to the top post upon the resignation of Eugene Lockhart, who left to become president of BankAmerica Corp's global retail bank.
Before joining MasterCard two and a half years ago, Selander had a 20-year career with Citicorp.

In the interview, Selander declined to comment on a continuing U.S. Department of Justice review of competitive practices in the card industry, other than to say "MasterCard is on a very sound basis right across the board."

The probe was launched following complaints by American Express Co that U.S. bylaws of the MasterCard and Visa organizations prohibit member banks from issuing cards on other networks. The Department is expected to announce results of its inquiry in April.
Referring to the growth prospects for cards versus cash and checks, Selander said "I see a tremendous industry opportunity to replace those older and frankly more costly ways to pay."

Discussing MasterCard's acquisition of a 51 percent stake in the Mondex cash system, a deal which closed last month, Selander said "Mondex does represent what we feel is an imporant continuation of our existing strategy."

Asked if he thought there was room for more than one technological system for smart cards, Selander said "there is a clear industry focus and desire to get to standards to insure that inter-operability is maintained."

The industry is planning several tests of smart card systems in coming months and one of the biggest is expected to begin in a section of New York City late this year. Selander said no one test would be the "be-all and end-all of what's going on" but rather the tests are part of a continuing process of learning and evolution."
He noted that chip cards got an early start in France where they are widely accepted with businesses finding them "an extremely secure and cost effective way of doing business."
Selander said MasterCard'd partnership with Europay and similar deals in Brazil and Argentina suggest that prospects for future growth of MasterCard's business are strong.
